areas.title: Practical life
areas.goal: Independence, coordinated movement, care of self and others.

areas.title: Sensorial
areas.goal: Careful comparison, sensory language, order and discrimination.

areas.title: Language
areas.goal: Conversation, sound awareness, writing, reading and meaning.

areas.title: Mathematics
areas.goal: Quantity, symbols, place value, operations and mathematical language.

areas.title: Cultural studies
areas.goal: Geography, living things, community, scientific inquiry and respect.

areas.title: Art, music & movement
areas.goal: Creative choices, rhythm, expression, movement and collaboration.

lessons.title: Carrying a tray
lessons.materials: Small tray; two stable, light objects
lessons.readiness: Can walk steadily and attend to a short demonstration.
steps: Hold opposite sides with two hands.
Walk slowly to a clear table and lower the tray quietly.
Return the tray and invite the child to try.
lessons.interest: Keeping the tray level.
lessons.control: Objects shift when the tray tilts.
lessons.observe: Grip, balance, walking pace and placement.
lessons.nextStep: Carry a tray with an empty pitcher.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Carry and place a tray with controlled movement.

lessons.title: Rolling and unrolling a work rug
lessons.materials: Small washable rug; open floor space
lessons.readiness: Can grasp with both hands.
steps: Unroll the rug slowly in a clear space.
Kneel at the short edge and turn a small fold evenly.
Roll with both hands and return it to its place.
lessons.interest: Matching the two edges.
lessons.control: Uneven edges show where the roll wandered.
lessons.observe: Chooses a clear space; rolls and stores the rug.
lessons.nextStep: Walk around another person’s work.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Prepare and restore a defined floor workspace.

lessons.title: Dry pouring
lessons.materials: Two small pitchers; large dry items; tray
lessons.readiness: Can grasp a pitcher and carry a tray.
steps: Show the starting and receiving pitchers.
Pour slowly, stopping before the second pitcher overflows.
Return spills to the tray and reset the work.
lessons.interest: Starting and stopping the flow.
lessons.control: Spills and items left in the starting pitcher are visible.
lessons.observe: Grip, wrist control and response to spills.
lessons.nextStep: Pour a small amount of water.
lessons.safety: Use large nonfood items if mouthing is possible. Assess choking risk and supervise; do not use beans with children who mouth objects.
lessons.aim: Transfer dry material by pouring with controlled starts and stops.

lessons.title: Pouring water
lessons.materials: Two small pitchers; a little water; tray; sponge
lessons.readiness: Has practiced controlling a dry pour.
steps: Lift the pitcher with a steady grip and aim at the opening.
Pour slowly and stop before the container fills.
Set it down and sponge up spills.
lessons.interest: The stream entering the opening.
lessons.control: Water outside the pitcher is visible.
lessons.observe: Flow control, stopping and cleanup without distress.
lessons.nextStep: Pour to a marked line.
lessons.safety: Use room-temperature water and immediately dry wet floors.
lessons.aim: Transfer water and manage small spills with growing independence.

lessons.title: Transferring with a spoon
lessons.materials: Two bowls; spoon; large transfer objects; tray
lessons.readiness: Can grasp and release a spoon.
steps: Place the bowls and spoon within easy reach.
Scoop, move over the receiving bowl and tip gently.
Continue, collect spills and reset.
lessons.interest: Keeping the spoon level.
lessons.control: A missed transfer is visible on the tray.
lessons.observe: Hand control and whether the spoon suits the child.
lessons.nextStep: Transfer with child-sized tongs.
lessons.safety: Select objects that are safe for this child; assess mouthing and choking risk.
lessons.aim: Transfer objects with a spoon using coordinated movement.

lessons.title: Using tongs
lessons.materials: Easy-squeeze tongs; large soft objects; two bowls
lessons.readiness: Can squeeze and release with one hand.
steps: Open the tongs around one object.
Squeeze gently, move it and release over the other bowl.
Continue and return the work in order.
lessons.interest: Squeezing enough to hold without crushing.
lessons.control: A dropped object shows that the grip needs adjustment.
lessons.observe: Grip, release and willingness to adjust.
lessons.nextStep: Use tongs in snack preparation.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Transfer objects by controlling the grip and release of tongs.

lessons.title: Handwashing sequence
lessons.materials: Accessible sink; soap; safe drying method
lessons.readiness: Can reach the setup with safe support.
steps: Wet hands, apply soap and rub all hand surfaces.
Use the program’s health guidance for thorough washing and rinsing.
Dry hands and leave the sink ready for the next person.
lessons.interest: Washing between fingers and over thumbs.
lessons.control: Soap or water left on hands can be seen or felt; cleanliness still requires adult guidance.
lessons.observe: Sequence and support needed at transitions.
lessons.nextStep: Use the sequence before food and after toileting.
lessons.safety: Provide safe access and supervision. Follow applicable health rules; this lesson does not replace required hygiene procedures.
lessons.aim: Carry out an effective handwashing routine with appropriate adult support.

lessons.title: Buttoning frame
lessons.materials: Buttoning frame with large buttons
lessons.readiness: Interested in fastening; can coordinate both hands.
steps: Hold the fabric near one button.
Guide the button through the opening and draw the fabric flat.
Repeat slowly, then show how to undo it.
lessons.interest: Turning the button to fit the hole.
lessons.control: Misaligned edges or an unfastened button are visible.
lessons.observe: Two-hand coordination and persistence.
lessons.nextStep: Use the skill on the child’s own clothing.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Fasten and unfasten buttons using coordinated hands.

lessons.title: Zipping frame
lessons.materials: Separating zipper frame
lessons.readiness: Can stabilize one side while moving the other.
steps: Show the bottom pieces meeting.
Insert the pin fully while holding the slider steady.
Pull the slider upward, then reverse and separate.
lessons.interest: Seating the pin before pulling.
lessons.control: The zipper will not close smoothly if it is not seated.
lessons.observe: Whether the child needs help starting or only pulling.
lessons.nextStep: Practice on a coat with permission.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Join and separate a zipper with controlled two-hand movement.

lessons.title: Washing a table
lessons.materials: Small basin; water; cloth; mild approved soap; drying cloth
lessons.readiness: Can carry water with support and follow a short sequence.
steps: Prepare the table and wet the cloth.
Wash in an orderly pattern, rinse and wipe.
Dry the surface and restore all materials.
lessons.interest: Seeing where the cloth has already traveled.
lessons.control: Visible wet or soapy patches guide another wipe.
lessons.observe: Order, coordination and restoring the workspace.
lessons.nextStep: Invite a child to care for a shared snack table.
lessons.safety: Use approved products and safe water amounts. Adults handle disinfectants and required sanitation.
lessons.aim: Care for a table through a complete orderly cleaning sequence.

lessons.title: Sweeping a small spill
lessons.materials: Child-sized broom; dustpan; large safe debris
lessons.readiness: Can manage a broom without hitting others.
steps: Mark or notice the small area to gather.
Sweep inward with controlled strokes.
Hold the pan, collect debris and return tools.
lessons.interest: Bringing scattered pieces to one place.
lessons.control: Pieces left on the floor remain visible.
lessons.observe: Tool control and checking the area afterward.
lessons.nextStep: Sweep a larger defined area.
lessons.safety: Keep others clear. Adults handle broken glass, bodily fluids and hazardous spills.
lessons.aim: Gather a small safe spill using a broom and dustpan.

lessons.title: Preparing a simple snack
lessons.materials: Washed soft fruit; safe spreading tool; plate; handwashing access
lessons.readiness: Can follow food hygiene routines with supervision.
steps: Wash hands and prepare a clean work area.
Demonstrate one safe preparation action slowly.
Serve an appropriate portion and clean the workspace.
lessons.interest: A careful, useful action that produces food to share.
lessons.control: Uneven portions can be compared; food safety needs adult oversight.
lessons.observe: Hygiene, tool use, portion awareness and cleanup.
lessons.nextStep: Prepare a snack with a peer.
lessons.safety: Check allergies and choking risks. An adult supervises tools and follows food safety rules; never use a tasting activity as an allergy test.
lessons.aim: Prepare and serve a simple snack using safe routines.

lessons.title: Inviting someone and respecting “no”
lessons.materials: Two willing participants; optional role-play puppets
lessons.readiness: Can communicate through words, signs or another supported method.
steps: Approach without touching another person’s work.
Offer a simple invitation and wait.
Model accepting either answer calmly and choosing another activity.
lessons.interest: Waiting for the other person’s choice.
lessons.control: The other person’s response provides feedback; an adult supports interpretation.
lessons.observe: Consent, waiting and alternate communication.
lessons.nextStep: Practice joining play at a natural pause.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Offer an invitation and respect another person’s decision.

lessons.title: Resolving a disagreement
lessons.materials: Quiet space; optional feeling cards
lessons.readiness: Can take a short turn with adult support; feels safe.
steps: Describe what happened without blame and ensure safety.
Invite each child’s account without forcing speech or an apology.
Offer workable choices, agree on a next step and check back.
lessons.interest: Listening to different accounts.
lessons.control: The agreed solution is checked in real use; adult guidance remains necessary.
lessons.observe: Words used, adult support and whether the solution worked.
lessons.nextStep: Practice a calm request before a conflict escalates.
lessons.safety: Stop aggression and protect children first. Do not require a child to mediate bullying or unsafe behavior.
lessons.aim: Take part in a supported, respectful solution to a disagreement.

lessons.title: Pink tower
lessons.materials: Ten graded cubes; work rug
lessons.readiness: Can carry a cube safely and compare noticeably different sizes.
steps: Carry cubes one at a time and spread them on the rug.
Build from largest to smallest with deliberate placement.
Compare the completed tower and return cubes in order.
lessons.interest: Centering each smaller cube.
lessons.control: The visual sequence and stability reveal many size errors.
lessons.observe: Compares size, carries carefully and notices changes.
lessons.nextStep: Grade three cubes with a larger contrast first.
lessons.safety: Never stack above a safe working height or allow cubes to be thrown.
lessons.aim: Visually grade cubes by changing size.

lessons.title: Brown stair
lessons.materials: Ten graded prisms; rug
lessons.readiness: Has compared size; can lift the larger prisms safely.
steps: Lay prisms apart where all can be seen.
Arrange thickest to thinnest with ends aligned.
Look along the stair and restore the set.
lessons.interest: Equal length with changing thickness.
lessons.control: An uneven progression is visible.
lessons.observe: Discriminates thickness rather than overall length.
lessons.nextStep: Compare thick and thin using two contrasting prisms.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Visually grade prisms by thickness.

lessons.title: Red rods
lessons.materials: Graded length rods; large clear rug
lessons.readiness: Can carry a long object safely and has space to work.
steps: Carry one rod horizontally with awareness of others.
Arrange longest to shortest with one end aligned.
Trace the changing lengths and return rods carefully.
lessons.interest: Finding the next length.
lessons.control: Misordered ends interrupt the visible progression.
lessons.observe: Length comparison and safe spatial awareness.
lessons.nextStep: Build a sequence with fewer widely different rods.
lessons.safety: Keep a generous clear space; adult help may be needed with long rods.
lessons.aim: Visually grade rods by length.

lessons.title: Cylinder blocks
lessons.materials: One cylinder block; stable table
lessons.readiness: Can use the knob comfortably.
steps: Remove cylinders with a light grasp and place them randomly.
Choose one, compare its size with a hole and lower it gently.
Continue, then invite repetition.
lessons.interest: A cylinder fitting flush in its opening.
lessons.control: A cylinder may not fit, or another is left without its matching opening.
lessons.observe: Visual comparison, grip and gentle handling.
lessons.nextStep: Introduce a second block after sustained interest.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Match cylinder dimensions with corresponding openings.

lessons.title: Color matching
lessons.materials: A small set of contrasting paired color tablets
lessons.readiness: Can attend to a two-object comparison.
steps: Handle tablets by their edges.
Place one tablet and find its matching color.
Lay pairs together, name colors after matching and restore.
lessons.interest: Finding the same color.
lessons.control: A mismatched pair can be visually compared.
lessons.observe: Matches before naming; note lighting and access needs.
lessons.nextStep: Add more color pairs.
lessons.safety: Offer accessible alternatives for visual differences; do not treat color naming as an intelligence measure.
lessons.aim: Match identical colors before emphasizing color names.

lessons.title: Color grading
lessons.materials: One family of graded color tablets
lessons.readiness: Can match similar colors and enjoys fine comparison.
steps: Place the darkest and lightest shades apart.
Select the next shade and make a continuous series.
Review the transitions and adjust if needed.
lessons.interest: Very small changes in shade.
lessons.control: An abrupt shade change invites comparison.
lessons.observe: Compares adjacent shades and revises choices.
lessons.nextStep: Grade a second color family in good natural light.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Order related colors by small differences in shade.

lessons.title: Geometric cabinet: matching shapes
lessons.materials: A few inset shapes with matching frames
lessons.readiness: Can manage knobs and compare outlines.
steps: Remove one inset and trace its edge with two fingers.
Trace the matching frame and fit the inset gently.
Repeat with two or three contrasting shapes.
lessons.interest: The edge and the space share an outline.
lessons.control: The inset fits its matching frame.
lessons.observe: Tracks an edge and compares shape without forcing.
lessons.nextStep: Match insets to outline cards.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Compare and match geometric outlines.

lessons.title: Touch tablets
lessons.materials: Paired texture tablets; handwashing access
lessons.readiness: Can choose to touch materials and communicate comfort.
steps: Explore two textures lightly with fingertips.
Compare another tablet and find the matching texture.
Pair tablets, then offer language such as rough and smooth.
lessons.interest: A light touch reveals texture.
lessons.control: Paired textures can be checked again by touch; some comparisons need adult discussion.
lessons.observe: Touch preference and ability to compare.
lessons.nextStep: Order a small series from smoother to rougher.
lessons.safety: Do not require blindfolding or touch. Respect sensory boundaries; check for skin irritation.
lessons.aim: Compare textures through a comfortable tactile experience.

lessons.title: Sound cylinders
lessons.materials: Paired sealed sound cylinders
lessons.readiness: Can handle materials gently and tolerate the sounds.
steps: Shake one cylinder gently near the body, away from ears.
Listen to another and compare.
Place matching pairs together and use the set’s check marks afterward.
lessons.interest: Listening to one sound at a time.
lessons.control: Matching marks, if provided, check the pairing after listening.
lessons.observe: Auditory comparison and volume regulation.
lessons.nextStep: Compare louder and softer sounds.
lessons.safety: Keep containers securely sealed and volume comfortable. Offer visual or vibration alternatives for hearing access.
lessons.aim: Match sounds through careful listening.

lessons.title: Geometric solids
lessons.materials: Sphere, cube and cylinder; mat
lessons.readiness: Interested in handling and comparing shapes.
steps: Explore one solid with hands and eyes.
Compare how another rests or rolls.
Name a small set through a three-period language lesson.
lessons.interest: Flat and curved surfaces behave differently.
lessons.control: The object’s movement gives feedback; names need a supportive adult check.
lessons.observe: Uses sensory descriptions and notices differences.
lessons.nextStep: Find a corresponding shape in the room.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Recognize and describe familiar geometric solids.

lessons.title: Conversation and precise naming
lessons.materials: Real objects or clear photographs related to the child’s life
lessons.readiness: Any spoken, signed or supported communication level.
steps: Invite the child to notice a real object.
Offer its precise name and pause for a response.
Expand one idea without demanding repetition.
lessons.interest: A familiar object has a useful name.
lessons.control: Meaningful conversation provides feedback; naming is not self-correcting.
lessons.observe: Initiation, vocabulary, home-language strengths and communication supports.
lessons.nextStep: Make a small vocabulary basket from an interest.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Build meaningful vocabulary through real conversation.

lessons.title: Three-period vocabulary lesson
lessons.materials: Two or three already explored objects
lessons.readiness: Attends to short interactions and can indicate a choice.
steps: Name each object simply: this is a sphere.
Ask the child to show or move a named object in varied ways.
Only when recognition is secure, invite the child to name it.
lessons.interest: Moving and finding known objects.
lessons.control: Adult observation guides a return to naming; do not quiz through repeated errors.
lessons.observe: Recognition separately from recall.
lessons.nextStep: Repeat with another small vocabulary set.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Connect a small set of words with familiar objects.

lessons.title: Sound game: beginning sounds
lessons.materials: Two or three familiar objects with clear starting sounds
lessons.readiness: Understands the object names; can attend to sound play.
steps: Name the objects naturally.
Say a starting sound without adding a vowel and invite a match.
Play briefly, then use the sound in another familiar word.
lessons.interest: Hearing a sound inside a spoken word.
lessons.control: An adult models the sound and supports comparison.
lessons.observe: Sound awareness separately from letter knowledge.
lessons.nextStep: Notice ending sounds after beginning sounds are secure.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Identify a beginning sound in a familiar spoken word.

lessons.title: Sound game: segmenting words
lessons.materials: A few familiar short words; optional counters
lessons.readiness: Can identify some individual spoken sounds.
steps: Say a short word slowly without distorting it.
Help the child listen for each sound in order.
Use one counter per heard sound and blend the word again.
lessons.interest: A word can be taken apart and joined again.
lessons.control: An adult checks spoken sound order; do not use letter count as a substitute.
lessons.observe: Sounds heard and support required.
lessons.nextStep: Build the same word with a movable alphabet.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Hear and sequence individual sounds in a short spoken word.

lessons.title: Sandpaper letters
lessons.materials: Two or three contrasting sandpaper letters
lessons.readiness: Shows sound awareness and tolerates the texture.
steps: Trace in the direction used for writing while saying the sound.
Invite tracing with the child’s preferred hand.
Use a brief three-period lesson to revisit the sound-symbol link.
lessons.interest: The movement and sound happen together.
lessons.control: Texture guides tracing; an adult supports direction and sound accuracy.
lessons.observe: Sound-symbol link, movement and comfort.
lessons.nextStep: Find a matching sound in a familiar object name.
lessons.safety: Offer a smooth or visual alternative if the texture is uncomfortable. Letter forms and sounds should suit the language being taught.
lessons.aim: Connect a speech sound with its written form and tracing movement.

lessons.title: Metal insets
lessons.materials: Inset frame; colored pencils; paper
lessons.readiness: Can hold a drawing tool comfortably with support if needed.
steps: Stabilize a frame and trace inside its boundary.
Trace the matching inset to compare the outlines.
Fill with controlled lines, adapting length to endurance.
lessons.interest: An outline closes and lines stay within a chosen shape.
lessons.control: Visible lines provide feedback; comfort and movement need adult observation.
lessons.observe: Light pressure, bilateral coordination and endurance.
lessons.nextStep: Combine two outlines for a design.
lessons.safety: Avoid forced pencil grips or long repetitive tracing sessions.
lessons.aim: Explore controlled lines and outlines with a comfortable drawing movement.

lessons.title: Movable alphabet: encoding words
lessons.materials: Movable alphabet; familiar objects or ideas
lessons.readiness: Can hear several sounds and recognizes corresponding symbols.
steps: Choose a meaningful spoken word.
Say its sounds slowly and select corresponding letters.
Read the sounds together and discuss the intended word.
lessons.interest: Writing an idea before pencil control is fully developed.
lessons.control: The spoken word can be compared with the letters; an adult supports conventional spelling.
lessons.observe: Sound representation, confidence and intended meaning.
lessons.nextStep: Build a phrase from a child’s own idea.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Represent a meaningful word through selected sound symbols.

lessons.title: Phonetic word reading
lessons.materials: Decodable words using known sound-symbol patterns; objects
lessons.readiness: Can blend sounds and knows the symbols used.
steps: Show one short word without a picture clue.
Invite sound blending, allowing processing time.
Match the decoded word to the object and discuss its meaning.
lessons.interest: The printed word carries a message.
lessons.control: Object matching supports meaning; an adult checks accurate decoding.
lessons.observe: Decoding separately from guessing from pictures.
lessons.nextStep: Read a short meaningful phrase with known patterns.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Decode a familiar-pattern word and connect it with meaning.

lessons.title: Phonograms and common spelling patterns
lessons.materials: A small matched set of phonogram cards and decodable words
lessons.readiness: Can read simple words with known correspondences.
steps: Introduce one spelling pattern with its sound.
Read a few words using that pattern.
Sort or build words and use one in a meaningful sentence.
lessons.interest: More than one letter can represent a sound.
lessons.control: A checked word set and adult modeling support accuracy.
lessons.observe: Pattern recognition, blending and transfer.
lessons.nextStep: Revisit the pattern in an appropriate decodable text.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Read and apply a new sound-spelling pattern.

lessons.title: Puzzle words / high-frequency words
lessons.materials: A few useful words with untaught or unusual spellings
lessons.readiness: Has a developing decoding foundation.
steps: Say and discuss one useful word.
Identify regular sound-spelling parts and point out the unexpected part.
Read and use it in a short phrase, then revisit later.
lessons.interest: Noticing the part that needs special attention.
lessons.control: A model card and adult feedback support checking.
lessons.observe: Recognition in a phrase, not only on an isolated card.
lessons.nextStep: Find the word in a short appropriate text.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Read a useful word while attending to its unusual spelling part.

lessons.title: Reading action commands
lessons.materials: Simple action slips using readable words
lessons.readiness: Can decode the words and understands the actions.
steps: Offer one short printed action privately.
Invite the child to read and carry out the safe action.
Discuss meaning, then let the child choose another slip.
lessons.interest: Print can invite an action without spoken directions.
lessons.control: The action can be compared with the message by child and adult.
lessons.observe: Comprehension beyond word pronunciation.
lessons.nextStep: Write a command for a willing peer.
lessons.safety: Avoid unsafe movement, food commands or actions that require unwanted touch.
lessons.aim: Read a short message and demonstrate its meaning through a safe action.

lessons.title: Noun and article exploration
lessons.materials: Familiar objects; phrase slips; grammar symbols if used
lessons.readiness: Reads simple phrases and can discuss familiar objects.
steps: Read a phrase naming an object.
Explore which word names the thing and which small word helps introduce it.
Match phrases to objects and discuss the words’ jobs.
lessons.interest: A word has a job in a meaningful phrase.
lessons.control: Object matching and adult discussion check meaning.
lessons.observe: Meaningful word-function awareness rather than memorized labels.
lessons.nextStep: Explore an adjective that changes which object is meant.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Explore the naming function of words within meaningful phrases.

lessons.title: Sentence reading and comprehension
lessons.materials: Short child-relevant sentences with accessible spelling patterns
lessons.readiness: Can read phrases with growing ease.
steps: Read a short sentence together or independently.
Ask what happened, allowing spoken, drawn or acted responses.
Return to the sentence to find evidence for the response.
lessons.interest: The whole message matters.
lessons.control: The text and adult discussion support checking.
lessons.observe: Accuracy, fluency, comprehension and enjoyment separately.
lessons.nextStep: Read a short connected text.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Read a sentence and communicate its meaning.

lessons.title: Storytelling and making a book
lessons.materials: Paper; drawing tools; optional adult scribe
lessons.readiness: Has an idea to communicate by speech, signs, drawing or print.
steps: Invite a real or imagined event.
Help arrange a beginning, a development and an ending without taking over.
Record the child’s words with permission and share the finished book.
lessons.interest: An idea becomes a book another person can understand.
lessons.control: The child checks whether the record expresses the intended story.
lessons.observe: Sequence, vocabulary, authorship and preferred communication.
lessons.nextStep: Add a page or reread to a chosen listener.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Organize and record an original story in an accessible form.

lessons.title: Number rods
lessons.materials: Ten alternating-color number rods; rug
lessons.readiness: Can grade lengths and is interested in counting.
steps: Build the length series with ends aligned.
Touch and count each section of a selected rod once.
Name its whole quantity and compare with another rod.
lessons.interest: A quantity stays together as one rod.
lessons.control: Length and colored sections support counting checks.
lessons.observe: One-to-one counting and quantity recognition.
lessons.nextStep: Match known rods to number symbols.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Connect counted sections with a whole quantity.

lessons.title: Sandpaper numerals
lessons.materials: Two or three sandpaper numerals
lessons.readiness: Understands some spoken quantities and enjoys symbol exploration.
steps: Trace one numeral in its writing direction while naming it.
Invite the child to trace or observe.
Use a short three-period lesson with contrasting numerals.
lessons.interest: Movement is connected to a number name.
lessons.control: Texture guides movement; adult observation checks name and direction.
lessons.observe: Symbol recognition separately from counting.
lessons.nextStep: Match numerals to counted quantities.
lessons.safety: Provide a nontextured alternative when needed.
lessons.aim: Recognize and trace familiar numeral symbols.

lessons.title: Number rods and numerals
lessons.materials: Number rods; corresponding numeral cards
lessons.readiness: Knows several rod quantities and numeral names.
steps: Choose a rod and count its sections.
Find its matching numeral and place it beside the rod.
Check by recounting and compare another pair.
lessons.interest: A written symbol stands for a quantity.
lessons.control: Recounting sections supports a check; an adult confirms symbols.
lessons.observe: Quantity-symbol correspondence and self-checking.
lessons.nextStep: Mix a small set of numerals and rods.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Match a known quantity with its numeral.

lessons.title: Spindle boxes and zero
lessons.materials: Spindle boxes labeled zero through nine; complete spindle set
lessons.readiness: Counts small quantities and recognizes numerals zero to nine.
steps: Read a compartment’s numeral.
Count that many spindles into a group and place them inside.
Leave zero empty and notice whether any spindles remain.
lessons.interest: Zero means no items in that compartment.
lessons.control: The exact set total reveals many counting errors.
lessons.observe: One-to-one counting, grouping and meaning of zero.
lessons.nextStep: Recheck any remaining spindles together.
lessons.safety: Assess small-part safety and supervise materials appropriately.
lessons.aim: Build separate quantities and explore zero as no objects.

lessons.title: Cards and counters: odd and even
lessons.materials: Numerals one to ten; complete counter set
lessons.readiness: Can count to ten and match quantities to symbols.
steps: Order the numerals and count counters beneath each.
Arrange counters in pairs, placing an unmatched one below.
Compare groups with and without an unmatched counter.
lessons.interest: Some quantities pair completely.
lessons.control: The counter arrangement makes an unmatched one visible.
lessons.observe: Accurate quantity and recognition of pairing.
lessons.nextStep: Discuss odd and even using the arrangement.
lessons.safety: Use counters suitable for the child and assess choking risk.
lessons.aim: Represent quantities in pairs and notice odd/even arrangements.

lessons.title: Golden beads: decimal quantities
lessons.materials: Unit bead; ten bar; hundred square; thousand cube
lessons.readiness: Understands counting to ten and can compare quantities.
steps: Explore each quantity category one at a time.
Count or compare ten of one category with one of the next.
Name the categories and invite the child to bring one.
lessons.interest: Ten of a category makes one of the next.
lessons.control: Material structure and guided counting support checking.
lessons.observe: Quantity language and comparisons before symbol demands.
lessons.nextStep: Associate large number cards with the quantities.
lessons.safety: Assess small-part risk. Use robust materials and close supervision as needed.
lessons.aim: Explore units, tens, hundreds and thousands as related quantities.

lessons.title: Decimal symbols and composition
lessons.materials: Large number cards; golden bead quantities
lessons.readiness: Recognizes the decimal quantity categories.
steps: Introduce category cards in a small set.
Build a quantity and choose the matching cards.
Overlay cards to form the number, then separate them to show place value.
lessons.interest: A number is made from separate quantity categories.
lessons.control: Comparing the bead categories with the cards supports checking.
lessons.observe: Place value rather than naming a long number by rote.
lessons.nextStep: Read and build a different number with a zero category.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Connect decimal quantities with written place-value symbols.

lessons.title: Golden bead static addition
lessons.materials: Golden beads; number cards; trays; prepared quantities
lessons.readiness: Can compose decimal quantities and combine small sets.
steps: Build two quantities that do not require exchanging.
Bring like categories together and count each total.
Choose result cards and describe joining the quantities.
lessons.interest: Two collections become one total.
lessons.control: Rebuilding and recounting check the result; an adult verifies the setup.
lessons.observe: Combining, category order and result explanation.
lessons.nextStep: Repeat independently before introducing exchanges.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Combine two concrete quantities without exchanges.

lessons.title: Golden bead exchange and dynamic addition
lessons.materials: Golden beads; cards; exchange supply
lessons.readiness: Understands static addition and ten-to-one relationships.
steps: Combine two prepared quantities.
When ten of a category accumulate, exchange them for one of the next.
Recount and represent the total with cards.
lessons.interest: An exchange changes the form, not the amount.
lessons.control: Compare the total before and after exchanging with adult support.
lessons.observe: Exchange reasoning and keeping categories aligned.
lessons.nextStep: Compose another total needing one exchange.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Combine quantities and preserve value through decimal exchanges.

lessons.title: Golden bead subtraction
lessons.materials: Golden beads; cards; a prepared whole and amount to remove
lessons.readiness: Understands taking away and can compose the starting quantity.
steps: Build the starting whole.
Remove the requested quantity into another space.
Count what remains and explain the change.
lessons.interest: The remaining collection represents the difference.
lessons.control: Put the removed amount back to check the starting whole.
lessons.observe: Meaning of subtraction and accurate removal.
lessons.nextStep: Introduce a needed exchange only after a clear concrete foundation.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Represent taking away and identify what remains.

lessons.title: Golden bead multiplication
lessons.materials: Golden beads; identical quantity trays; cards
lessons.readiness: Can combine quantities and recognize equal groups.
steps: Prepare a small number of equal groups.
Combine like categories and find the total.
Describe the repeated equal quantity using the appropriate language.
lessons.interest: Each group starts with the same amount.
lessons.control: Reconstruct equal groups to check the total.
lessons.observe: Equal groups separately from a memorized fact.
lessons.nextStep: Use another small equal-group example.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Explore multiplication through combining equal groups.

lessons.title: Golden bead sharing / division
lessons.materials: Golden beads; a divisible total; recipient markers
lessons.readiness: Understands equal sharing and concrete quantities.
steps: Set out the recipients and the whole collection.
Share one category fairly, exchanging only with guidance if appropriate.
Compare shares and state how much each receives.
lessons.interest: Each recipient receives the same amount.
lessons.control: Compare shares and recombine them to check the whole.
lessons.observe: Fair sharing, tracking recipients and remainder awareness.
lessons.nextStep: Try another exactly divisible quantity first.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Explore division through sharing a quantity equally.

lessons.title: Teen quantities and symbols
lessons.materials: Teen boards or cards; ten bars; unit beads
lessons.readiness: Understands ten and one-to-one counting beyond ten.
steps: Build ten and add one or more units.
Match the quantity to its teen symbol.
Count the whole and name the number without losing the group of ten.
lessons.interest: A teen number contains one ten and some units.
lessons.control: Compare the bar and units with the symbol; an adult checks naming.
lessons.observe: Teen naming, quantity and symbol as separate observations.
lessons.nextStep: Compare two teen numbers.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Connect a group of ten and extra units with a teen symbol.

lessons.title: Tens quantities and symbols
lessons.materials: Tens boards or cards; ten bars; units
lessons.readiness: Understands a ten bar and some teen quantities.
steps: Count ten bars as tens.
Match the quantity to the appropriate tens symbol.
Add units and compose a two-digit number.
lessons.interest: Tens stay grouped while units change.
lessons.control: Count bars and units against the cards.
lessons.observe: Counting by tens and composing without rote guessing.
lessons.nextStep: Build and read a child-chosen two-digit number.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Connect groups of tens and additional units with two-digit symbols.

lessons.title: Bead chains and skip counting
lessons.materials: A suitable bead chain; matching labels; long safe work space
lessons.readiness: Counts accurately and can sustain a longer sequence.
steps: Lay out a short chain and count each bead.
Place labels at repeated group boundaries.
Review the repeating group size and connect it with equal groups.
lessons.interest: A regular numerical pattern appears.
lessons.control: Count back along the chain and compare labels; guided checks may be needed.
lessons.observe: Accurate tracking, sequence and recognition of equal groups.
lessons.nextStep: Choose a longer chain when endurance and interest support it.
lessons.safety: Keep walkways clear and assess bead safety.
lessons.aim: Explore counting sequences and repeated equal groups.

lessons.title: Fraction insets: whole and equal parts
lessons.materials: Fraction circles or equal-part insets
lessons.readiness: Can compare shapes and discuss a whole.
steps: Explore a whole circle, then replace it with two equal parts.
Compare equal parts with other equal divisions.
Name simple fractions in relation to the same whole.
lessons.interest: Equal parts recombine into the whole.
lessons.control: Insets fill the same frame without gaps or overlaps.
lessons.observe: Equal partitioning and the relationship to the whole.
lessons.nextStep: Compare one-half and one-fourth of the same-sized whole.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Explore a whole divided into equal parts.

lessons.title: Land, water and globe exploration
lessons.materials: Land-and-water globe; plain map; small land/water photos
lessons.readiness: Interested in the world and can explore a model.
steps: Explore the globe’s land and water surfaces.
Find examples in photographs and compare them.
Explain that the globe is a small model of Earth.
lessons.interest: A model represents a much larger place.
lessons.control: Model and photos support comparison; adult dialogue checks meaning.
lessons.observe: Model understanding and land/water language.
lessons.nextStep: Explore a continent globe.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Recognize a globe as a model of Earth’s land and water.

lessons.title: Continents: shapes and names
lessons.materials: Continent globe; puzzle map; diverse place photographs
lessons.readiness: Understands globe as a model of Earth.
steps: Relate the flat map to the globe.
Explore and name a small number of continents.
Connect a continent to real places and varied communities.
lessons.interest: A shape on the map represents real places.
lessons.control: Puzzle outlines support placement; names require guided checking.
lessons.observe: Location, model awareness and respectful questions.
lessons.nextStep: Investigate one place connected to a child’s family.
lessons.safety: Present political and cultural information thoughtfully; do not equate one continent with one language or culture.
lessons.aim: Relate continent shapes on a globe and a flat map to real places.

lessons.title: Landforms: island and lake
lessons.materials: Safe landform trays; small amount of water; photos
lessons.readiness: Can pour with support and compare land with water.
steps: Add a little water to an island model.
Compare a lake model and notice what surrounds what.
Match each model to a real photograph and name it.
lessons.interest: The surrounding material changes the landform.
lessons.control: Models and photographs support checking with an adult.
lessons.observe: Explains what surrounds land or water.
lessons.nextStep: Explore another contrasting landform pair.
lessons.safety: Use shallow water under supervision and empty trays after use.
lessons.aim: Compare island and lake models with real landforms.

lessons.title: Living and nonliving inquiry
lessons.materials: Photos or safely observed examples; sorting spaces
lessons.readiness: Interested in plants, animals and everyday objects.
steps: Observe a few clear examples of living things.
Discuss growth and needs across time, not movement alone.
Sort clear examples and keep uncertain cases for inquiry.
lessons.interest: Living things have needs and change over time.
lessons.control: Adult-supported evidence checks the sort; a moving object is not necessarily living.
lessons.observe: Reasoning and questions rather than a memorized answer.
lessons.nextStep: Observe a plant’s changes over several days.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Use observations to explore characteristics of living things.

lessons.title: Parts and care of a plant
lessons.materials: Healthy non-toxic plant; plant diagram; care tools
lessons.readiness: Can handle a plant gently.
steps: Observe roots if visible, stem and leaves without damaging them.
Name parts and connect each with a simple function.
Provide the plant’s actual care and record what changes.
lessons.interest: The parts work together in a real plant.
lessons.control: A diagram supports names; the plant’s condition informs care over time.
lessons.observe: Care decisions, vocabulary and close observation.
lessons.nextStep: Draw and label the observed plant.
lessons.safety: Select non-toxic species; check allergies and avoid unknown plants or soil ingestion.
lessons.aim: Connect plant parts with their functions and care.

lessons.title: Seed germination observation
lessons.materials: Safe seeds; clear container; suitable growing medium; observation sheets
lessons.readiness: Can follow a simple care routine.
steps: Prepare a few seeds using suitable growing conditions.
Observe regularly and draw what is actually visible.
Compare changes without inventing a result or fixed growth date.
lessons.interest: A change can be recorded before it can be explained.
lessons.control: Dated observations allow comparisons; a seed may not germinate.
lessons.observe: Descriptive language, patience and evidence.
lessons.nextStep: Compare one carefully changed growing condition with adult guidance.
lessons.safety: Do not eat experimental seeds. Check mold, allergies and small-part risks; wash hands.
lessons.aim: Record actual changes in a growing seed over time.

lessons.title: Animal classification and needs
lessons.materials: Accurate animal pictures; small classification set
lessons.readiness: Recognizes several animals and enjoys comparison.
steps: Compare a few animals by an observable feature.
Introduce a limited, accurate grouping and relevant vocabulary.
Discuss varied needs and habitats without treating all members as identical.
lessons.interest: A grouping helps us notice shared features.
lessons.control: Reliable reference pictures and adult review check the grouping.
lessons.observe: Uses evidence and recognizes exceptions when introduced.
lessons.nextStep: Investigate one animal in more detail.
lessons.safety: Do not bring unknown wildlife into the classroom or require animal handling.
lessons.aim: Compare animals using a limited, accurate set of shared features.

lessons.title: Magnetic and nonmagnetic materials
lessons.materials: Large encased magnet; safe test objects; two trays
lessons.readiness: Can follow handling limits and make a prediction.
steps: Predict whether one object will be attracted.
Test it slowly and observe without changing the claim afterward.
Group results and try another object of a different material.
lessons.interest: A prediction may differ from the result.
lessons.control: The test outcome is observable; repeat to confirm.
lessons.observe: Prediction, actual result and descriptive language.
lessons.nextStep: Compare different safe metal objects.
lessons.safety: Use a large, intact encased magnet under direct supervision. Never use loose high-powered magnets or objects that can be swallowed.
lessons.aim: Make and test predictions about magnetic attraction.

lessons.title: Weather journal
lessons.materials: Window or safe outdoor space; weather symbols; dated journal
lessons.readiness: Can make a brief daily observation.
steps: Look at the actual sky and surroundings.
Record what is observed using a drawing, symbol or dictated note.
Compare records after several days without predicting a fixed pattern.
lessons.interest: A record helps remember yesterday accurately.
lessons.control: The journal can be compared with current observations; past entries are evidence, not forecasts.
lessons.observe: Observation separate from prediction.
lessons.nextStep: Compare clothing choices with the actual conditions.
lessons.safety: Follow outdoor weather, air quality and sun-safety procedures.
lessons.aim: Record and compare daily observations of local weather.

lessons.title: Personal timeline and change
lessons.materials: Optional family-approved photos or child drawings; timeline strip
lessons.readiness: Interested in personal history; comfortable sharing.
steps: Invite the child to select events they want to share.
Arrange a few events in meaningful order.
Discuss what has changed and what remains important.
lessons.interest: A sequence represents the passage of time.
lessons.control: Family information and the child’s account support checking.
lessons.observe: Temporal words and respect for different family stories.
lessons.nextStep: Make a timeline of a classroom project.
lessons.safety: Participation and family photos are optional. Respect adoption, loss, privacy and varied family structures.
lessons.aim: Arrange personally meaningful events in a sequence.

lessons.title: Community helpers and real roles
lessons.materials: Local photographs; books; optional invited visitor
lessons.readiness: Interested in how people help a community.
steps: Ask what the child has noticed people doing.
Explore several real roles using inclusive examples.
Connect a role with tools, choices and ways children can ask for help.
lessons.interest: Work has a purpose in the community.
lessons.control: Authentic accounts and reliable books support checking.
lessons.observe: Questions, vocabulary and avoiding stereotypes.
lessons.nextStep: Prepare respectful questions for a visitor.
lessons.safety: Follow visitor and safeguarding procedures; do not imply every uniformed person is automatically a safe contact.
lessons.aim: Explore real community roles without stereotypes.

lessons.title: Cultural inquiry with families
lessons.materials: Family-volunteered stories, music, objects or books
lessons.readiness: Shows interest; families choose what and whether to share.
steps: Invite a specific contribution without asking one family to represent a whole culture.
Explore the item and its meaning in that family’s own words.
Record questions and similarities without ranking traditions.
lessons.interest: People within the same culture can have different experiences.
lessons.control: The contributing family’s account and reliable sources guide interpretation.
lessons.observe: Respectful questions and language about similarities and differences.
lessons.nextStep: Explore another family’s perspective with consent.
lessons.safety: Do not use sacred items as dress-up props, require cultural disclosure or assign a child the role of cultural spokesperson.
lessons.aim: Explore a family’s shared experience with respect and curiosity.

lessons.title: Open-ended drawing
lessons.materials: Accessible drawing tools; paper; workspace
lessons.readiness: Interested in making marks.
steps: Show safe care of one drawing tool.
Invite the child to choose marks, colors and subject.
Offer descriptive feedback and let the child decide whether to keep or share.
lessons.interest: The child makes meaningful choices.
lessons.control: The child’s intention guides revision; there is no model to copy exactly.
lessons.observe: Choices, movement and the child’s own account.
lessons.nextStep: Offer a different drawing medium.
lessons.safety: Use intact, child-sized materials. Supervise according to the child and the activity.
lessons.aim: Make and communicate original drawing choices.

lessons.title: Cutting and collage
lessons.materials: Child-sized scissors; paper strips; paste; backing paper
lessons.readiness: Can follow scissor safety with appropriate support.
steps: Show how to carry, hold and close scissors safely.
Offer short strips to cut and a choice of placement.
Demonstrate a small amount of paste and invite an original composition.
lessons.interest: Cut pieces can be arranged in many ways.
lessons.control: The child decides the design; adult feedback supports safe tool use.
lessons.observe: Two-hand coordination, safe handling and artistic choices.
lessons.nextStep: Offer wider strips or a chosen simple line.
lessons.safety: Supervise scissors; use adaptive tools as needed and check paste ingredients.
lessons.aim: Use safe cutting and joining techniques in an original composition.

lessons.title: Clay and modeling
lessons.materials: Non-toxic modeling material; mat; simple blunt tools
lessons.readiness: Can handle material safely and does not mouth it.
steps: Show pressing, rolling and pinching as options.
Invite the child to explore and create without a required product.
Clean tools and hands and store the material correctly.
lessons.interest: Hands change the material’s form.
lessons.control: The child compares the form with their intention.
lessons.observe: Hand strength, sensory preference and chosen techniques.
lessons.nextStep: Make a form from an observation or story.
lessons.safety: Check ingredients and allergies; do not use food-based dough where it creates a risk. Supervise small pieces.
lessons.aim: Explore and shape a modeling material with chosen techniques.

lessons.title: Rhythm echo and choice
lessons.materials: Voice, clapping or a safe quiet percussion instrument
lessons.readiness: Can participate comfortably through movement, sound or observation.
steps: Offer a short comfortable rhythm.
Invite an echo or an alternative accessible response.
Let the child offer a pattern for a willing adult or peer.
lessons.interest: A pattern can be heard, felt or seen.
lessons.control: Listen or watch together; participation is not scored for perfection.
lessons.observe: Pattern noticing, turn taking and sound comfort.
lessons.nextStep: Combine a rhythm with a familiar song.
lessons.safety: Keep sound levels comfortable and offer a quiet opt-out.
lessons.aim: Notice, repeat or create a short rhythmic pattern.

lessons.title: Pitch comparison and singing
lessons.materials: Voice or tuned child-appropriate instrument; two contrasting pitches
lessons.readiness: Enjoys listening and can choose whether to join.
steps: Offer two comfortable contrasting pitches.
Invite listening, gesture or vocal exploration.
Sing a short familiar phrase and let the child choose a way to respond.
lessons.interest: Sounds can be higher or lower.
lessons.control: Comparison and adult modeling support listening; singing accuracy is not a judgment of musical worth.
lessons.observe: Listening, preference and willing participation.
lessons.nextStep: Explore another short melody.
lessons.safety: Avoid loud or strained singing; respect hearing and communication differences.
lessons.aim: Explore contrasting pitches and musical response.

lessons.title: Walking the line and expressive movement
lessons.materials: Clear floor line; optional gentle music
lessons.readiness: Can move in the space with safe support.
steps: Demonstrate careful walking with awareness of the space.
Invite chosen movement at a comfortable pace without requiring heel-to-toe perfection.
Offer a pause, notice others and return the space to order.
lessons.interest: Movement can be controlled and expressive.
lessons.control: Balance and spatial feedback guide adjustments.
lessons.observe: Coordination, self-regulation and participation choices.
lessons.nextStep: Offer a simple movement pattern or accessible seated alternative.
lessons.safety: Clear the floor, avoid slippery surfaces and provide mobility adaptations without penalty.
lessons.aim: Practice safe controlled and expressive movement with appropriate access.
